input: Claim: checkout.charge fans out to exactly 2 payment-provider calls for a 5-line-item cart, not N+1 per line item. Assertion: run the checkout flow with a 5-line-item cart, then count the payment-provider spans produced.
notes: Matches allowed kind 1 (span count) and the rule's own Correct example verbatim in shape.

input: Claim: the retry-wrapper span is always the parent of the underlying HTTP-call span. Assertion: run one request that triggers a retry, then check the retried span's parent reference points to the retry-wrapper span.
notes: Matches allowed kind 2 (parent/child structure) — decided by observing a run, not by reading source.

input: Claim: the cache-lookup span completes in under 5ms on a warm cache. Assertion: run a request against a warmed cache and read the recorded span duration.
notes: Matches allowed kind 3 (duration) — the bound can only be confirmed by an executed run.

input: Claim: the payment span's status flips to Error when the provider returns a 500. Assertion: run a request that forces a 500 from a test double and check the resulting span's status field.
notes: Matches allowed kind 4 (span status on the error path).

input: Claim: a single inbound checkout request produces exactly 3 outbound calls: inventory, payment, and shipping. Assertion: run one checkout and count the outbound child spans.
notes: Matches allowed kind 5 (downstream fan-out).

input: Claim: the user.id attribute on the request span has an unbounded set of distinct values across a load run, making it unsafe as a metric dimension. Assertion: run a load test and count the distinct user.id values observed across the run's spans.
notes: Matches allowed kind 6 (attribute cardinality) — the rule states this can be confirmed unbounded via an executed run.

input: Claim: the auth-check span always starts and ends before the db-query span begins. Assertion: run one authenticated request and compare the two spans' recorded start/end timestamps.
notes: Matches allowed kind 7 (ordering).

input: Claim: an upload that exceeds the size limit produces a span whose status is Error rather than Ok. Assertion: run an upload of an oversized file and read the resulting span's status.
notes: A second instance of allowed kind 4 (span status on the error path), phrased around a different operation than the file's own example.

input: Claim: checkout.charge emits a span. Assertion: grep the source for startSpan(\"checkout.charge\").
notes: This is the rule's own Incorrect example verbatim (a span named X exists, checked by grep).

input: Claim: the new instrumentation adds a span for the refund handler. Assertion: read the PR diff and confirm the refund handler file now contains a startSpan call.
notes: The discriminator question — could this be satisfied by reading source alone? — answers yes; this reads the diff, never a run.

input: Claim: the payment span records an amount attribute. Assertion: open the source file and check that the span-creation call sets an amount attribute key.
notes: Declares the attribute is set in source, never confirms it fires with a real value on an executed path.

input: Claim: the ingest job emits a batch.size span attribute. Assertion: without running anything, confirm the code declares .setAttribute(\"batch.size\", ...) at the span-creation call site.
notes: States explicitly 'without running anything' — the discriminator's own test names this by-construction directly.

input: Claim: the new order-created span is present. Assertion: statically confirm the tracer.startSpan(\"order-created\") call exists somewhere in the changed file, without executing the code.
notes: A static existence check on a span declaration, explicitly not executing the code — matches the forbidden pattern's own wording.

input: Claim: the checkout flow now has telemetry coverage. Assertion: search the diff for any call to startSpan and confirm at least one such call was added.
notes: A diff/source search for a span-creation call, never an executed run — the diff read back.

input: Claim: the order-created span is wired up. Assertion: run the full test suite, then grep the changed instrumentation file to confirm the startSpan(\"order.created\") call is present.
notes: DECOY (run-verb surface, static check). The run is a red herring — nothing about its outcome is read. The check is a source grep, so the discriminator's question ('satisfiable by reading source alone?') answers yes. Counters the keyword shortcut that every 'run' case is behavioral.

input: Claim: the refund span carries a refund.reason attribute. Assertion: execute the refund flow once, then confirm the span-builder call site in the source declares .setAttribute(\"refund.reason\", ...).
notes: DECOY (run-verb surface, static check). Executing the flow is discarded — the assertion inspects the declaration, never the emitted value, so a span that fired with an undefined attribute still passes. By-construction under the discriminator.

input: Claim: the cart-merge path now has telemetry coverage. Assertion: start the service under the OTLP proxy, then search the repository for any startSpan call inside the cart-merge module.
notes: DECOY (run-verb surface, static check). Booting under the proxy produces telemetry nobody reads; the coverage claim is settled by a repository search, which is the diff read back.

input: Claim: no db.query span is ever emitted as a root span — each one is a child of a request span. Assertion: grep the OTLP JSON the run exported and confirm no db.query span has a null parent id.
notes: DECOY (static-verb surface, executed evidence). 'grep' is the file's own by-construction tell, but the target is the EMITTED export, not source. Unanswerable by reading the code, so behavioral — allowed kind 2 (parent/child structure).

input: Claim: one checkout produces exactly one payment.charge span, not one per retry attempt. Assertion: grep the collector's output file from the previous checkout and count the payment.charge span entries.
notes: DECOY (static-verb surface, executed evidence). 'grep' and 'count' name no run, but the artifact grepped is what an execution emitted — allowed kind 1 (span count). Reading the source cannot settle how many fired.

input: Claim: the auth-check span always completes before the db-query span starts. Assertion: without running anything further, read the trace the last CI execution already recorded and compare the auth-check span's end timestamp against the db-query span's start timestamp.
notes: DECOY (static-verb surface, executed evidence). Opens with 'without running anything further' — near-verbatim the phrase case 12 uses to signal by-construction — yet the artifact read is an execution's trace, so the discriminator still answers 'no, source alone cannot settle this'. Allowed kind 7 (ordering); source order does not settle runtime order.

input: Claim: the notification fan-out produces one span per recipient, not one per batch. Assertion: send a batch of 4 notifications through the service, then count the per-recipient spans in the captured export.
notes: DECOY (no run vocabulary anywhere). Allowed kind 5 (fan-out). Counts spans an execution captured; source cannot settle one-per-recipient vs one-per-batch.

input: Claim: the import span's status is Error when the CSV has a malformed header. Assertion: submit a malformed CSV and read the status on the resulting span.
notes: DECOY (no run vocabulary anywhere). Allowed kind 4 (span status on the error path).

input: Claim: the session.id attribute stays bounded at 20 distinct values across a soak. Assertion: exercise the endpoint 500 times and count the distinct session.id values in the emitted spans.
notes: DECOY (no run vocabulary anywhere). Allowed kind 6 (attribute cardinality); boundedness is a property of what was emitted.

input: Claim: the cache-warm span always precedes the first query span. Assertion: issue one cold request and compare the two spans' timestamps in the captured trace.
notes: DECOY (no run vocabulary anywhere). Allowed kind 7 (ordering); declaration order in source does not settle emission order.

input: Claim: the webhook handler is instrumented. Assertion: run the service once, then confirm the handler file imports the tracer and calls startSpan.
notes: DECOY (run verb, static check). The run's output is never read; an import plus a call site is a source fact.

input: Claim: the queue-consumer span sets a queue.name attribute. Assertion: run the consumer once, then open the source and verify the attribute key is passed at the span-builder call.
notes: DECOY (run verb, static check). Verifies the key is passed in source, not that it was emitted with a value.

input: Claim: the new export path has telemetry. Assertion: run the integration suite, then grep the diff for added startSpan calls.
notes: DECOY (run verb, static check). A diff grep for span-creation calls is the diff read back; the suite result is discarded.

input: Claim: the startSpan call in the retry wrapper fires once per request, not once per attempt. Assertion: trigger a request that retries twice and count the wrapper spans in the captured export.
notes: DECOY (names startSpan, still behavioral). The literal is the by-construction tell, but the question is how many times it FIRED, which only an execution answers. Allowed kind 1 (span count).

input: Claim: the startSpan in the db layer always attaches to the active request span rather than starting a new trace. Assertion: issue one request and check the db span's parent in the emitted trace.
notes: DECOY (names startSpan, still behavioral). Allowed kind 2 (parent/child); whether context propagated is a runtime fact.

input: Claim: the audit path is instrumented. Assertion: read the instrumentation module and confirm a tracer is obtained and a span is created for the audit path.
notes: DECOY (by-construction without the startSpan literal). A source read for a span-creation site, phrased generically — the forbidden pattern does not depend on the API's spelling.

input: Claim: the billing span carries a tenant attribute. Assertion: inspect the tracing helper in source and confirm the tenant key is included in the attribute map it builds.
notes: DECOY (by-construction without the startSpan literal). Confirms the key is in a map in source; says nothing about what a run emitted.

input: Claim: the startSpan call in the batch importer fires once per imported file, not once per row. Assertion: import a 3-file batch, then grep the exported OTLP records for importer spans and confirm there are exactly 3.
notes: DECOY (wears BOTH by-construction surface tells — names startSpan and greps — and is still behavioral). Allowed kind 1 (span count): how many times a call FIRED is a runtime fact, and the artifact grepped is what the import emitted, not source.

input: Claim: the retry helper's startSpan produces a child of the caller's span, never a sibling. Assertion: trigger one retried call, then grep the collector's file for both span ids and check the parent reference on the retried one.
notes: DECOY (names startSpan and greps, still behavioral). Allowed kind 2 (parent/child structure): whether context propagated is decided at runtime, and the file grepped is an execution artifact.

input: Claim: every span on the ingest path carries a tenant attribute — none is emitted without one. Assertion: statically scan the NDJSON the last import exported and confirm every span record has a tenant key.
notes: DECOY (says 'statically', still behavioral). The scan targets the emitted export, not source: a setAttribute declared behind a conditional is present in source and absent from half the emitted spans, so only what ran settles this. Closest to allowed kind 6 (attribute cardinality).

input: Claim: the notifier's startSpan is invoked once per channel, so a 3-channel notification yields 3 child spans. Assertion: dispatch one 3-channel notification and count the child spans in the captured export.
notes: DECOY (names startSpan, carries no run verb either). Allowed kind 5 (downstream fan-out): the per-channel count is a property of the dispatch, not of the call site.

input: Claim: the cache layer is instrumented. Assertion: run the app once, then confirm in the PR diff that the cache module now wraps its lookup in a tracer call.
notes: DECOY (run verb, and none of the static-read tells — no grep, no 'statically', no startSpan literal). The run's output is never read; a wrapper visible in the diff is a source fact, so the discriminator answers 'yes, source alone settles it'.

input: Claim: the worker exports traces to the configured endpoint. Assertion: execute one job, then confirm the SDK setup file lists the OTLP exporter in its span-processor chain.
notes: DECOY (run verb, no static-read tell, no startSpan literal). Reads a configuration declaration; whether a span was actually exported — or dropped by a full queue — is never checked.

input: Claim: the audit handler emits a span with a correlation id. Assertion: confirm the handler passes a correlation-id attribute at the span-builder call site it declares.
notes: DECOY (wears NONE of the surface tells — no run verb, no startSpan literal, no static-read verb). Reads a declaration and says nothing about what any execution emitted.

input: Claim: the reporting module is traced. Assertion: check that the module imports the tracer factory and that a span wrapper is applied to its entry function.
notes: DECOY (wears none of the surface tells). An import plus a wrapper is a source fact; a wrapper on a function nothing calls still passes this assertion.
